title: Coil-built basket-weave texture bowl
subtitle: Building an air-dry clay bowl using coils, then impressing a woven basket pattern on the outer wall
excerpt: This air-dry bowl is coil-built from the base up and then textured by pressing a woven wicker or cane surface against the outer wall while the clay is still soft. The basket-weave pattern adds visual texture without carving. No kiln, no wheel.
sourceNotes: Coil-built basket-weave bowl for air-dry clay derived from first principles.

glossaryTerms.definition: A long rope of clay rolled between the palms, used as the building unit in coil construction
Roughening both clay surfaces with a needle and applying diluted clay before pressing coils together
The stage at which the wall holds its shape for textured impressions

content.text: A coil-built bowl is a series of clay rings stacked and blended together. Once the walls are built and smoothed, pressing a wicker mat, a cane place mat, or even a loosely woven hessian cloth against the outer surface prints the weave into the clay. The
leather-hard
stage is the right time for texturing , soft enough to take an impression clearly, firm enough not to distort.

items.name: Wicker mat, cane trivet, or woven hessian (for texture)
Small bowl to use as a former (optional)

content.text: Build the base
Pinch or roll a flat disc of clay 10-12 cm in diameter and 8 mm thick. This is the bowl base. Smooth the surface and edges with a rib.
Build the walls with coils
Roll a
coil
of clay about 15 mm in diameter and long enough to circle the base perimeter.
Score and slip
the top edge of the base. Place the first coil on top of the base, pressing down firmly. Blend the inner face of the join with a rib or finger. Leave the outer face unblended for now.

Continue adding coils, using score and slip on each layer. After every second coil, blend the inner face of the wall smooth to strengthen it. Aim for a finished height of 8-10 cm, flaring the wall diameter very slightly outward with each row to form a shallow bowl shape.
Once all coils are in place, blend the inner wall surface smooth with a rib. The outer wall can be left with the coil ridges visible or blended smooth before texturing.
Press in the basket-weave texture
Allow the bowl to firm to leather-hard. The outer wall should hold its shape without support.
Press the wicker mat or hessian cloth firmly against the outer wall section by section, pressing with your thumbs from behind the cloth. Hold for 10 seconds each section, then peel back.
Work around the bowl in sections, overlapping each slightly to keep the pattern continuous.
Finish and dry
Smooth the bowl rim with a damp sponge and bevel it very slightly inward , a flat-topped rim chips more easily than a rounded one.
Allow to dry slowly under a loose cloth for at least 24 hours. Once bone-dry, seal the inside and outside with two coats of PVA varnish.

items.solution: The inner blending was not thorough. At leather-hard stage, dampen the crack with a wet finger and press the clay back together, then re-blend with a rib.
Press the texture cloth in firmer, shorter sections. Move methodically around the wall and overlap each section slightly so the pattern does not break.
